title: America bet everything on trust 250 years ago. That bet is being tested again
excerpt: The future of free enterprise depends on rebuilding the trust that lets citizens, markets, institutions and allies work together.
content_html:
Keith Krach

Sat, August 1, 2026 at 4:30 AM MST 5 min read

A finance employee at the global design firm Arup transferred $25.6 million in a deepfake fraud after joining a video call with synthetic versions of senior executives. The faces looked real. The voices sounded real. The instructions were false.

That was not an isolated warning. Starbucks quietly retired an AI inventory system only nine months after deployment after baristas reported that it miscounted products and slowed their work. Deloitte's Australian member firm agreed to partially refund the government for a $290,000 AI-assisted report that included nonexistent academic sources and a fabricated court quotation. Different industries. Different technologies. The same failure: people could not trust the output, the identity, or the system.

Trust is becoming a form of economic infrastructure. Companies that cannot engineer it will move slower, spend more, and lose markets. When trust is strong, capital moves, partnerships form, and companies scale. When it breaks, transactions slow, compliance and insurance costs rise, and leaders retreat from risk.

Trust is not blind faith. It is earned confidence that facts are real, identities are authentic, systems are secure, contracts will be honored, and someone will be accountable when things go wrong. In business terms, trust reduces friction. In strategic terms, it creates speed.

America's original trust bet

As America marks its 250th anniversary, we should remember that trust was not a side note to the founding. It was the bet. In my first three essays in this Freedom & Enterprise series, I described the Declaration of Independence as America's first founding bet, the system it created as one that let people build free, and the freedom to fail as one of our greatest competitive advantages. Beneath all three is a more fundamental principle: America trusted free people to govern themselves, take risks, honor commitments, and build institutions strong enough to survive disagreement.

For most of history, order was imposed from above because rulers did not trust ordinary people with power. The Declaration reversed that logic. Its signers pledged their lives, fortunes, and sacred honor not only to reject a king, but to trust citizens they would never meet and generations they would never see. That trust became an economic advantage: entrepreneurs could start without royal permission, investors could back ideas because property rights and contracts mattered, and talent could rise by merit. The system was imperfect, but its capacity to correct itself and rebuild confidence became one of America's greatest strengths.

基思·克拉奇

2026 年 8 月 1 日星期六凌晨 4:30（MST） 阅读 5 分钟

全球设计公司奥雅纳 (Arup) 的一名财务员工在加入与合成版高级管理人员的视频通话后，通过深度造假诈骗转移了 2560 万美元。 这些面孔看起来很真实。 声音听起来很真实。 这些指示是错误的。

这并不是一个孤立的警告。 星巴克在部署人工智能库存系统仅九个月后就悄悄退役了，因为咖啡师报告称该系统错误计数了产品并减慢了工作速度。 德勤澳大利亚成员公司同意向政府部分退款 29 万美元的人工智能辅助报告，其中包括不存在的学术来源和捏造的法庭引文。 不同的行业。 不同的技术。 同样的失败：人们无法信任输出、身份或系统。

信任正在成为经济基础设施的一种形式。 无法设计它的公司将会行动缓慢、支出更多并失去市场。 当信任牢固时，资本就会流动，合作伙伴关系就会形成，公司就会扩大规模。 当它崩溃时，交易就会放缓，合规和保险成本就会上升，领导者就会回避风险。

信任不是盲目的信仰。 人们相信事实是真实的，身份是真实的，系统是安全的，合同将得到履行，出现问题时有人会承担责任。 从商业角度来说，信任可以减少摩擦。 从战略角度来说，它创造了速度。

美国最初的信任赌注

在美国庆祝建国 250 周年之际，我们应该记住，信任并不是建国的附注。 这是赌注。 在这个自由与企业系列的前三篇文章中，我将《独立宣言》描述为美国的第一个建国赌注，将其创建的体系描述为让人们自由建设的体系，将失败的自由描述为我们最大的竞争优势之一。 在这三者之下有一个更基本的原则：美国相信自由人民能够自我管理、承担风险、履行承诺并建立足够强大的机构来解决分歧。

在历史的大部分时间里，秩序都是自上而下强加的，因为统治者不信任普通人拥有权力。 《宣言》扭转了这一逻辑。 它的签署者承诺他们的生命、财富和神圣荣誉，不仅是为了拒绝国王，而且是为了信任他们永远不会见到的公民和他们永远不会见到的后代。 这种信任变成了一种经济优势：企业家可以在没有王室许可的情况下开始创业，投资者可以支持想法，因为产权和合同很重要，人才可以凭功绩而崛起。 该体系并不完美，但其自我纠正和重建信心的能力成为美国最大的优势之一。
